newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso recoups losses, ends stronger.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso recoups losses, ends stronger.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early weakness to close firmer on Monday, due to dealers unwinding long dollar positions and gains in the stock and money markets, traders said.

The benchmark 48-hour peso MXAAA and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.8770/7.8810 and 7.8710/7.8750 per dollar, respectively. The 48-hour peso had weakened 0.3 centavos to 7.891/7.896 per dollar at the start.
"Apparently some one in Chicago who was short in pesos and...stepped into the market to sell greenbacks," said a dealer.
The peso firmed up as some local and foreign investors stepped into the local stock and money markets, spurring other dealers to cover peso positions.
"The peso firmed up on dollar surpluses being sold and we expect the exchange rate to remain firm throughout the week," said a trader.
The Mexican stock market's leading IPC .MXX index was up 32.94 points, or 1.00 percent at 3,324.63 as the foreign exchange market closed.
Overnight Cetes rates were meanwhile down 100 basis points at 27.50 percent.
The same-day peso closed earlier 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.8810/7.8860 per dollar.
